# Repairs exercised by the final replay

The first run exposed an inherited negative control that set a pure helper route to the route it already had. The repaired test chooses two distinct width-nine owners, copies the complete owner entry to create a real collision, asserts that the mutation changed the input, and requires the direct ownership rule to reject overlapping physical footprints. No mathematical validity check was removed.

The new response kernel raises the backward scalar prefix envelope to 1,048,913, requiring 21 bits rather than the old fixture's 20. The independent invoice now derives its local prefix requirement from the exact replay. The global total is 206 bits; the retained 512-bit charge and row allowance remain sufficient. All strict finite and outer inequalities are checked anew.

After these repairs and the manifest/input newline changes, all 13 stages passed from scratch on a copy where every recognized text file had CRLF line endings. This is the delivered program, with the same exact exponent and canonical final template as the discovery replay. Original failed logs remain in the local research archive rather than being represented as successful runs.
